guides.name: DEEPX Compiler Solution
guides.title: DEEPX Compiler Solution
guides.intro: Compile an ONNX model into the DXNN format for DEEPX NPUs on AWS — interactively on an Amazon EC2 instance, or automatically with a CloudFormation stack that compiles every model you upload to Amazon S3. Both paths use the same compiler and calibration dataset, so the result is identical.

steps.title: Choose a deployment option
items: Open the [DEEPX Compiler Solution](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-ev6ed5omu4ulo) listing on AWS Marketplace. Its launch page offers two services.
**Amazon EC2** (custom deployment using an AMI): you start an instance and run the compiler yourself. Best for trying options repeatedly and interactive debugging.

**AWS CloudFormation** (automated, one-step deployment): you upload files to Amazon S3 and compilation starts on its own; the workflow starts and terminates the instance. Best for repeatable compilation and CI.

image.alt: The DEEPX Compiler Solution product page on AWS Marketplace

steps.title: Prerequisites
items: An AWS account with permissions to launch EC2 instances or create a CloudFormation stack.
The ONNX model and its JSON configuration file. Validated models and configurations are available in the [DEEPX Model Zoo](https://developer.deepx.ai/modelzoo/).
An existing VPC and subnet that reach Amazon S3, AWS Systems Manager and Amazon CloudWatch Logs over HTTPS. A private subnet needs a NAT gateway or VPC endpoints.
To run AWS CLI commands from your machine, configure credentials once. If `aws sts get-caller-identity` prints your account ID and user ARN, you are ready.
commands:
aws configure
# AWS Access Key ID [None]: <access-key-id>
# AWS Secret Access Key [None]: <secret-access-key>
# Default region name [None]: <region, for example us-east-1>
# Default output format [None]: json

aws sts get-caller-identity

sections.title: Path A — Compile on Amazon EC2

steps.title: Subscribe and launch an instance
items: On the product page, choose **View purchase options** and subscribe.
On **Launch DEEPX Compiler Solution**, set **Service** to **Amazon EC2**.

Under **Launch method**, choose **One-click launch from AWS Marketplace**. Use **Launch from EC2 Console** only when you need options the form does not expose, such as an instance profile, user data or extra volumes.
Fill in **Version** (the latest stable `dx-com` release is preselected), **Region**, **Number of instances**, **Instance type**, **VPC**, **Subnet**, **Security group** and **Key pair**.
Choose **Launch**.
steps.note: Compilation is CPU- and memory-intensive. The launch page marks `t3.xlarge` (4 vCPUs, 16 GiB) as **Vendor recommended**; larger models or more calibration images may run faster on a larger type. The security group needs no inbound access beyond SSH.

image.alt: Launch configuration with Service set to Amazon EC2

steps.title: Connect and prepare the model
items: In **EC2 › Instances**, find the instance's address and connect over SSH as `ubuntu`.
Activate the compiler's Python environment. The compiler and the calibration dataset are preinstalled under `/opt/dx-compiler`.
Download the model and its Model Zoo configuration, then point `dataset_path` at the calibration dataset bundled in the AMI.
steps.note: Start from the Model Zoo configuration: a hand-written file without the `preprocessings` list fails. The calibration images are one level deeper than the AMI documents: `/opt/dx-compiler/calibration_dataset/calibration_dataset`.
commands:
ssh -i <your-key>.pem ubuntu@<instance-address>

source /opt/dx-compiler/venv/bin/activate

curl -fLO https://sdk.deepx.ai/modelzoo/onnx/yolov5-s-face_640x640.onnx
curl -fLO https://sdk.deepx.ai/modelzoo/q-lite-json/2_4_0/yolov5-s-face_640x640.json

sed -i 's#"dataset_path": *"[^"]*"#"dataset_path": "/opt/dx-compiler/calibration_dataset/calibration_dataset"#' \
    yolov5-s-face_640x640.json

steps.title: Run the compilation
items: Run `dxcom` with the model (`-m`), the configuration (`-c`) and the output directory (`-o`). It is on `PATH` only while the `(venv)` environment is active.
The compiler prints its configuration, quantization and preprocessing decisions, then a progress bar.
steps.note: A `GPU device discovery failed` warning at the start is harmless: the instance has no GPU and compilation falls back to CPU.

image.alt: Compiling the ONNX model with dxcom on the EC2 instance

commands:
dxcom -m yolov5-s-face_640x640.onnx \
      -c yolov5-s-face_640x640.json \
      -o output/yolov5-s-face_640x640

steps.title: Check the output and upload it
items: The `.dxnn` file is written inside the `-o` directory, named after the model.
Upload it to Amazon S3 so edge devices and other environments can download it.

image.alt: The compiled .dxnn file in the output directory

commands: ls -lhR output/
aws s3 cp output/yolov5-s-face_640x640/yolov5-s-face_640x640.dxnn s3://<your-bucket>/<path>/

steps.title: Terminate the instance
items: In **EC2 › Instances**, select the compiler instance.
Choose **Instance state › Terminate instance** to stop the charges. Delete any EBS volume that is not deleted with the instance.
If you compile often, Path B is easier to manage and costs nothing while idle.

steps.title: Launch the stack from the listing
items: Subscribe on the product page (**View purchase options**) if you have not already.
On **Launch DEEPX Compiler Solution**, set **Service** to **AWS CloudFormation** and choose the Region.
Launch it. The CloudFormation console opens on **Create stack** with the template already selected.

steps.title: Enter the stack parameters
items: Enter a **Stack name** (letters, numbers and hyphens).
`ImageId` — the SSM parameter path of the DX Compiler AMI. It resolves to the AMI of the Region; keep the default.
`ModelBucketName` — the S3 bucket for `.onnx`/`.json` inputs and `.dxnn` results. It must be globally unique.
`InstanceType` — the compiler instance type. The default is `t3.xlarge`.
`VpcId` / `SubnetId` — the existing VPC and subnet for the compiler instance, with outbound HTTPS to AWS services.
steps.note: The screenshot comes from the Greengrass stack, which adds `ThingGroupName` and runtime fields. The Compiler stack shows only the AMI, network, instance and storage groups.

image.alt: Specify stack details in the CloudFormation console

steps.title: Create the stack and read its outputs
items: Choose **Next**, keep the stack options, then on the review page choose **Submit**. If asked, acknowledge that CloudFormation may create IAM resources.
Wait until the stack reaches **CREATE_COMPLETE**. It creates the model bucket, Lambda functions, the Step Functions state machine and least-privilege IAM roles.
On the **Outputs** tab, note `ModelBucketName`, `StateMachineArn` and `CompilerExecutionLogGroupName`.

image.alt: The stack at CREATE_COMPLETE

steps.title: Upload the .onnx and .json to S3
items: In **S3 › Buckets**, open the `ModelBucketName` bucket.
Choose **Create folder** and create `models/<model-name>/` — one dedicated folder per model.
Open the folder, choose **Upload › Add files**, add the `.onnx` model and its `.json` configuration with the same base name, and choose **Upload**.
Compilation starts only when both files are in the same folder. The CLI commands below do the same from a terminal.
steps.note: Whatever `dataset_path` the configuration holds, the pipeline replaces it with the calibration dataset bundled in the AMI (`/opt/dx-compiler/calibration_dataset`).

image.alt: The model and its configuration uploaded to the same S3 path

commands:
export STACK_NAME=<cloudformation-stack-name>

export MODEL_BUCKET=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks \
  --stack-name "$STACK_NAME" \
  --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='ModelBucketName'].OutputValue" \
  --output text)

export MODEL_PREFIX=models/yolov5-s-face_640x640

curl -fLO https://sdk.deepx.ai/modelzoo/onnx/yolov5-s-face_640x640.onnx
curl -fLO https://sdk.deepx.ai/modelzoo/q-lite-json/2_4_0/yolov5-s-face_640x640.json

aws s3 cp --only-show-errors yolov5-s-face_640x640.onnx "s3://${MODEL_BUCKET}/${MODEL_PREFIX}/"
aws s3 cp --only-show-errors yolov5-s-face_640x640.json "s3://${MODEL_BUCKET}/${MODEL_PREFIX}/"

steps.title: Watch the Step Functions workflow
items: In **Step Functions › State machines**, open the state machine from `StateMachineArn` and select the newest execution.
The graph shows the instance starting, the compile command running through Systems Manager, status polling and the instance terminating. It terminates the instance on failure too.
Wait for **Succeeded**. Detailed `dxcom` logs are in CloudWatch Logs under `/dx-compiler/<stack-name>/execution`.

image.alt: The compilation workflow in the Step Functions console

commands:
export STATE_MACHINE_ARN=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks \
  --stack-name "$STACK_NAME" \
  --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='StateMachineArn'].OutputValue" \
  --output text)

aws stepfunctions list-executions \
  --state-machine-arn "$STATE_MACHINE_ARN" \
  --max-results 5 \
  --query "executions[].[status,startDate,stopDate,name]" \
  --output table

export COMPILER_LOG_GROUP=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks \
  --stack-name "$STACK_NAME" \
  --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='CompilerExecutionLogGroupName'].OutputValue" \
  --output text)

aws logs tail "$COMPILER_LOG_GROUP" --since 1h --follow

steps.title: Download the .dxnn
items: Back in the model folder of the bucket, the compiled `.dxnn` sits next to the source `.onnx` and `.json`.
Select it and choose **Download**, or copy it with the CLI.

image.alt: The compiled .dxnn in the same S3 path as the source model

commands:
aws s3 ls "s3://${MODEL_BUCKET}/${MODEL_PREFIX}/"
# yolov5-s-face_640x640.onnx
# yolov5-s-face_640x640.json
# yolov5-s-face_640x640.dxnn
aws s3 cp "s3://${MODEL_BUCKET}/${MODEL_PREFIX}/yolov5-s-face_640x640.dxnn" .

steps.title: Cost
items: Software pricing and subscription terms are on the AWS Marketplace listing; AWS resource charges apply separately.

**Amazon EC2 and EBS**: the compiler instance and its volumes while they run. The CloudFormation pipeline runs the instance only during a job; an instance you launch yourself runs until you terminate it.
**Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, AWS Step Functions, Amazon CloudWatch Logs** (CloudFormation path): storage, events, workflow runs and log retention.
Estimate with the [AWS Pricing Calculator](https://calculator.aws/) before you deploy.

steps.title: Clean up
items: EC2 path: terminate the instance and delete any leftover EBS volumes.
CloudFormation path: in **CloudFormation › Stacks**, select the stack and choose **Delete**.
The model bucket is kept to protect your data. If you no longer need it, empty it and delete it in the S3 console.
Cancel the subscription in [Manage subscriptions](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/library) if you no longer need it.

steps.title: Troubleshooting
items: **The workflow does not start after an upload** — both the `.onnx` and the `.json` must be in the same S3 path; with only one, the trigger waits.
**The workflow fails** — read the `dxcom` logs in the `/dx-compiler/<stack-name>/execution` log group.
**The instance does not launch** — check that the subnet has outbound HTTPS (NAT gateway or VPC endpoints) and that the subscription is complete.
**`dxcom: command not found`** — run `source /opt/dx-compiler/venv/bin/activate` first.
**Calibration images not found** — `dataset_path` must be `/opt/dx-compiler/calibration_dataset/calibration_dataset`, not its parent.
**Input shape error or low accuracy** — make `inputs` match the ONNX model, and `preprocessings` match training; raise `calibration_num` if needed.

guides.name: DEEPX Greengrass Solution
guides.title: DEEPX Greengrass Solution
guides.intro: One CloudFormation stack provides the cloud compile pipeline and deploys the DEEPX runtime (NPU driver, firmware, dx_rt and dx_stream) over the air to every Greengrass core device in a Thing Group.

steps.title: How the solution works
items: In the cloud, uploading an `.onnx` and its `.json` to the same S3 prefix triggers AWS Lambda, which starts a Step Functions workflow. It launches a temporary EC2 instance from the DEEPX Compiler AMI, runs `dxcom` through Systems Manager Run Command, stores the `.dxnn` next to the source and terminates the instance.

At the edge, the stack publishes the `com.deepx.dx-runtime` Greengrass component and deploys it to a Thing Group. Every core device in the group installs the NPU driver, firmware, dx_rt and dx_stream and reports the result.
Adding a registered device to the Thing Group is enough to provision it (zero-touch provisioning). Certificate injection at manufacturing or fleet provisioning needs a separate design.

image.alt: Cloud compile pipeline and Greengrass runtime deployment

steps.title: Prerequisites
items: An AWS account with permissions to create a CloudFormation stack.
An edge device with a DEEPX DX-M1 M.2 module, for example a Raspberry Pi 5 (arm64) or an x86_64 Ubuntu host.
The ONNX model and its JSON configuration — for example from the [DEEPX Model Zoo](https://developer.deepx.ai/modelzoo/).
An existing VPC and subnet for the compiler instance, with outbound HTTPS to Amazon S3, AWS Systems Manager and Amazon CloudWatch Logs (NAT gateway or VPC endpoints for a private subnet).

steps.title: Subscribe on AWS Marketplace
items: In AWS Marketplace, search for [DEEPX Greengrass Solution](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-732s46qfzuh34), select it and subscribe.
Choose the AWS Region to deploy in and choose **Launch with CloudFormation**.
Need compilation only, without device deployment? Use the DEEPX Compiler Solution guide instead.

image.alt: The DEEPX solution subscription page on AWS Marketplace

steps.title: Enter the stack parameters
items: Enter a **Stack name**.
`ImageId` — the SSM parameter path of the DX Compiler AMI; keep the default.
`ModelBucketName` — the S3 bucket for ONNX inputs and DXNN results; globally unique.
`InstanceType` — the compiler instance type; default `t3.xlarge`.
`VpcId` / `SubnetId` — the existing VPC and subnet for the compiler instance, with outbound HTTPS to AWS services.
`ThingGroupName` — the Thing Group that receives the runtime. Leave it blank to create `<stack-name>-cores`; enter an existing group's name to use that group.

image.alt: Specify stack details in the CloudFormation console

steps.title: Create the stack and read its outputs
items: Choose **Next** to reach the review page, then choose **Submit**. If asked, acknowledge that CloudFormation may create IAM resources.
The stack creates the model bucket, Lambda functions, the Step Functions state machine, least-privilege IAM roles, and the Greengrass component and deployment. Wait for **CREATE_COMPLETE**.
On **Outputs**, note `ModelBucketName`, `StateMachineArn`, `CompilerExecutionLogGroupName`, `ThingGroupName` and `TokenExchangeRoleName`.

image.alt: The stack at CREATE_COMPLETE

steps.title: Upload the .onnx and .json to S3
items: In **S3 › Buckets**, open the `ModelBucketName` bucket and create a dedicated folder per model, such as `models/yolov5-s-face_640x640/`.
Choose **Upload › Add files**, add the `.onnx` model and the `.json` configuration with the same base name, and choose **Upload**.
Use the Model Zoo configuration of the model. The pipeline replaces its `dataset_path` with the calibration dataset bundled in the AMI.

image.alt: The model and its configuration uploaded to the same S3 path

commands:
export STACK_NAME=<cloudformation-stack-name>

export MODEL_BUCKET=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks \
  --stack-name "$STACK_NAME" \
  --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='ModelBucketName'].OutputValue" \
  --output text)

export MODEL_PREFIX=models/yolov5-s-face_640x640

curl -fLO https://sdk.deepx.ai/modelzoo/onnx/yolov5-s-face_640x640.onnx
curl -fLO https://sdk.deepx.ai/modelzoo/q-lite-json/2_4_0/yolov5-s-face_640x640.json

aws s3 cp --only-show-errors yolov5-s-face_640x640.onnx "s3://${MODEL_BUCKET}/${MODEL_PREFIX}/"
aws s3 cp --only-show-errors yolov5-s-face_640x640.json "s3://${MODEL_BUCKET}/${MODEL_PREFIX}/"

steps.title: Watch the Step Functions workflow
items: In **Step Functions › State machines**, open the state machine from `StateMachineArn` and select the newest execution.
The workflow starts the instance, runs the compilation, polls for status and terminates the instance — on failure paths too.
In the `/dx-compiler/<stack-name>/execution` log group you should see the S3 download, the `dxcom` run and the `.dxnn` upload in that order.

image.alt: The compilation workflow at Succeeded

commands:
export STATE_MACHINE_ARN=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks \
  --stack-name "$STACK_NAME" \
  --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='StateMachineArn'].OutputValue" \
  --output text)

aws stepfunctions list-executions \
  --state-machine-arn "$STATE_MACHINE_ARN" \
  --max-results 5 \
  --query "executions[].[status,startDate,stopDate,name]" \
  --output table

export COMPILER_LOG_GROUP=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks \
  --stack-name "$STACK_NAME" \
  --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='CompilerExecutionLogGroupName'].OutputValue" \
  --output text)

aws logs tail "$COMPILER_LOG_GROUP" --since 1h --follow

steps.title: Find the .dxnn in S3
items: The compiled `.dxnn` appears in the same S3 folder as the source model.
No compile server runs in between: the EC2 instance exists only while a job runs.

image.alt: The compiled .dxnn in the same S3 path as the source model

commands:
aws s3 ls "s3://${MODEL_BUCKET}/${MODEL_PREFIX}/"
# yolov5-s-face_640x640.onnx
# yolov5-s-face_640x640.json
# yolov5-s-face_640x640.dxnn

sections.title: Deploy the runtime to a device

steps.title: Register the device as a Greengrass core
items: On the device, install Java 11 or later and provide AWS credentials allowed to provision Greengrass (IoT thing, certificate and policy, IAM role alias). Use long-term IAM user keys for development only.
Download the AWS IoT Greengrass Core software and install it with the stack outputs: `--thing-group-name` is `ThingGroupName` and `--tes-role-name` is `TokenExchangeRoleName`.
Check that the service runs, then in **IoT Greengrass › Core devices** confirm the device is **Healthy**.
steps.note: Joining the Thing Group is what triggers the runtime deployment. Any device already registered can be added to the group instead.
commands:
curl -s https://d2s8p88vqu9w66.cloudfront.net/releases/greengrass-nucleus-latest.zip -o greengrass-nucleus-latest.zip
unzip greengrass-nucleus-latest.zip -d GreengrassInstaller

sudo -E java -Droot="/greengrass/v2" -Dlog.store=FILE \
  -jar ./GreengrassInstaller/lib/Greengrass.jar \
  --aws-region <region> \
  --thing-name <thing-name> \
  --thing-group-name <ThingGroupName> \
  --tes-role-name <TokenExchangeRoleName> \
  --component-default-user ggc_user:ggc_group \
  --provision true \
  --setup-system-service true
sudo systemctl status greengrass.service

steps.title: Watch the com.deepx.dx-runtime deployment
items: In **IoT Greengrass › Deployments**, open **<stack-name> DX Runtime Deployment**. It targets the Thing Group and starts for every core device in it.

Greengrass delivers the component as an AWS IoT job over TLS-secured MQTT. The device downloads the packages over HTTPS and installs the NPU driver (`dxrt-driver-dkms`), dx_rt (`libdxrt-bin`), the firmware (`fw.bin` via `dxcli -u`) and dx_stream.
Wait until each device shows **Succeeded**. If one reports a problem, read the component log on the device.
To roll out a new runtime version later, raise the component version and create a new deployment for the Thing Group.
steps.note: Installation time depends on the device and the network. Low-spec arm64 devices that build libraries from source can take tens of minutes or more.

image.alt: Deployment status of the target devices

commands:
# Classic Greengrass nucleus
sudo tail -f /greengrass/v2/logs/com.deepx.dx-runtime.log

# Greengrass nucleus lite
sudo journalctl -f -u ggl.com.deepx.dx-runtime.service

steps.title: Check the NPU on the device
items: Run `dxcli -s` to see the detected NPU and its firmware version.

image.alt: dxcli -s output with the detected NPU and firmware version

commands: dxcli -s

steps.title: Check the dx_stream plugin
items: Set the dx_stream executable and library paths. The snippet picks the plugin directory for x86_64 or aarch64; add it to `~/.bashrc` to keep it for every shell.
`gst-inspect-1.0 dxstream` lists the registered dx_stream elements.

image.alt: gst-inspect-1.0 dxstream listing the registered elements

commands:
GST_ARCH_TRIPLET="$(gcc -dumpmachine 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$GST_ARCH_TRIPLET" ]; then
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) GST_ARCH_TRIPLET="x86_64-linux-gnu" ;;
    aarch64|arm64) GST_ARCH_TRIPLET="aarch64-linux-gnu" ;;
    armv7l|armv6l) GST_ARCH_TRIPLET="arm-linux-gnueabihf" ;;
    *) GST_ARCH_TRIPLET="$(uname -m)-linux-gnu" ;;
  esac
fi

GST_PLUGIN_DIR="/usr/local/lib/$GST_ARCH_TRIPLET/gstreamer-1.0"
export GST_PLUGIN_PATH="$GST_PLUGIN_DIR:$GST_PLUGIN_PATH"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$GST_PLUGIN_DIR:/usr/local/share/gstdxstream/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"
export PATH="/usr/local/share/gstdxstream/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"

gst-inspect-1.0 dxstream

steps.title: Run a test inference
items: The stack deploys the runtime; compiled models stay in S3. Copy the `.dxnn` to the device for this test. Deploying models over the air needs a separate Greengrass component.

Download the sample video and run the pipeline: `dxpreprocess` resizes frames to 640×640, `dxinfer` runs the NPU, `dxpostprocess` decodes YOLOv5s-Face results, `dxosd` draws the boxes and `fpsdisplaysink` shows them with the frame rate.
steps.note: Post-processing is model specific. With another model, change `library-file-path` together with `model-path`.

image.alt: Face detection running in DEEPX dx_stream

commands: aws s3 cp "s3://${MODEL_BUCKET}/${MODEL_PREFIX}/yolov5-s-face_640x640.dxnn" .

curl -fSLO https://sdk.deepx.ai/res/video/sample_videos.tar.gz
tar xzf sample_videos.tar.gz

export MODEL_PATH="$PWD/yolov5-s-face_640x640.dxnn"
export INPUT_VIDEO_PATH="$PWD/dance-group.mov"
export VIDEOCONVERT_PIPELINE="videoconvert"

gst-launch-1.0 urisourcebin uri=file://$INPUT_VIDEO_PATH ! decodebin ! \
  dxpreprocess preprocess-id=1 resize-width=640 resize-height=640 ! \
  queue max-size-buffers=1 ! \
  dxinfer preprocess-id=1 inference-id=1 model-path=$MODEL_PATH ! \
  queue max-size-buffers=1 ! \
  dxpostprocess inference-id=1 \
  library-file-path=/usr/local/share/gstdxstream/lib/libpostprocess_yolov5s_face.so \
  function-name=PostProcess ! \
  queue max-size-buffers=1 ! dxosd ! \
  $VIDEOCONVERT_PIPELINE ! fpsdisplaysink sync=false

steps.title: Cost
items: Software pricing and subscription terms are on the AWS Marketplace listing; AWS resource charges apply separately.
**Amazon EC2**: the compiler instance runs only during a compilation and is terminated on success and failure, so you pay only for compile time.
**Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, AWS Step Functions, Amazon CloudWatch Logs**: storage, events, workflow runs and log retention.
**AWS IoT Core and AWS IoT Greengrass**: depend on the features you use and the number of devices.
Estimate with the [AWS Pricing Calculator](https://calculator.aws/) before you deploy.

steps.title: Clean up
items: In **CloudFormation › Stacks**, select the stack and choose **Delete**. The Thing Group and component versions it created go with it; a pre-existing group it used is kept.
The model bucket is kept to protect your data. If you no longer need it, empty it and delete it.
Cancel the subscription in [Manage subscriptions](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/library) if you no longer need it.
Optional: revise the deployment in the Greengrass console to remove the component from your devices.
